facts.statement: Day count conventions define how accrued interest is calculated: Actual/Actual for Treasury bonds, 30/360 for corporate/municipal bonds, and Actual/360 for money market instruments.
Cash Price (Dirty Price) equals Quoted Clean Price plus Accrued Interest: Cash Price = Quoted Price + Accrued Interest.
CBOT Treasury bond futures allow delivery of any Treasury bond with remaining maturity >= 15 years, non-callable for >= 15 years. Prices quote in points and 32nds.
The Conversion Factor (CF) is the theoretical clean price of $1.00 face value of the bond if its yield to maturity were exactly 6.0% semi-annual.
Invoice Price received by seller upon physical bond delivery is: Invoice Price = (Most Recent Settlement Price * Conversion Factor) + Accrued Interest.
The Cheapest-to-Deliver (CTD) bond minimizes Net Cost = Quoted Cash Price - (Futures Price * Conversion Factor).
When market yields > 6%, low-coupon long-maturity bonds tend to be CTD; when market yields < 6%, high-coupon short-maturity bonds tend to be CTD.
The Wild Card play exploits the settlement price being fixed at 2:00 PM while notice of intention to deliver can be filed up to 8:00 PM Chicago time.
With futures settlement price $90.00, CF = 1.2000, and accrued interest $2.50 per $100 par, Invoice Price = ($90.00 * 1.2000) + $2.50 = $108.00 + $2.50 = $110.50.

realWorldProblem.actors: Fixed income institutional traders, Treasury primary dealers, and bond portfolio managers
realWorldProblem.situation: Hedging multi-billion dollar sovereign bond portfolios and calculating delivery obligations under CBOT futures
realWorldProblem.failure: Misidentifying the Cheapest-to-Deliver bond or miscalculating conversion factor adjustments creates fatal delivery losses
realWorldProblem.invention: Conversion Factor equalization system, CTD optimization algorithms, and Wild Card delivery options
